audit.whatIsWrong: Six of seven chart rows disagreed with their own whys[] line and with the already-audited mirror: win[0] said Wukong where the why says level 1 is even, win[1] and win[2] gave stages to Skill/Cho'Gath where the whys hand them to you, win[3] said Cho'Gath where the why says even, win[4] said Wukong on the row the why gives to Feast, and win[6] said Cho'Gath where the why says skill.
audit.why: The chogath__wukong mirror audit fixed this chart as Skill / Wukong / Wukong / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Skill with ratings 5,4,4,5,6,6,5 from his side — 5,6,6,5,4,4,5 from yours. The packet levelChart is identical and so is the prose already on this page.
audit.corrected: Rows 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 flipped in BOTH layers as matched pairs; ratings inverted from the mirror's.

audit.whatIsWrong: Not one cooldown on the page, and the header data disagreed with itself — diff "HARD" next to a 4/10 difficulty, a green tone, and a report line reading "Favoured matchup".
audit.why: Rupture is 6s flat at 950 range, Feral Scream is 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s, Feast is 80/70/60s. Those three numbers are the whole lane: a 6s Rupture means the sidestep window comes back constantly, while an 80s Feast means one dodged ultimate buys you a full wave. The mirror rates the lane EVEN at 5.5/10, not favoured at 4/10.
audit.corrected: Cooldowns written into the cooldown block, dosFull[0].d, phases[0].why, phases[2].why, phases[3].why, phases[4].why and spikes[1].text; diff, tone, diffRating and the two difficulty lines aligned to the mirror's EVEN 5.5/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Feral Scream's silence appears only as a don't-title ("Get silenced mid-combo") whose description is unrelated boilerplate, and Feast's true damage was never stated as such.
audit.why: The silence is the decisive interaction: it denies Warrior Trickster AND Nimbus Strike, so a Wukong caught in the cone has neither an engage nor an escape for its duration. And Feast deals true damage — the entry's Plated Steelcaps and armour-shred framing implies resistances help against it, and they do not.
audit.corrected: dontsFull[1].d now states the 11s silence and what it shuts off; Feast's true damage stated in phases[4].why and spikes[1].text.

edits.before: Q-AA poke wins the short exchanges. Identify how Cho'Gath contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Rupture is 950 range and 6s flat, but you have no all-in yet — even farming, and don't stand in the telegraph.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Cho'Gath must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit at 3 — Crushing Blow shreds his armour and cuts his regen, so E in, land it, and clone out before Rupture's delay ends.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Rupture's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: Even: he farms safely with Vorpal Spikes and edges toward Feast. Trade only on the 6s after Rupture, and bank your lead.

edits.before: Cyclone’s double knockup wins every committed brawl. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Cho'Gath's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Feast is 80s at rank 1 and deals true damage — armour does nothing, so stay above its threshold and refuse the all-in.

edits.before: Two items on: your side-lane pattern is at full power. Cho'Gath carry threat 6/10 — close before the map decides instead of you.
edits.after: Two items in it settles to skill: he out-tanks your duel, you out-manoeuvre him — use Cyclone to peel, not to solo him.

edits.before: - Cho'Gath Rupture: matchup-defining — Telegraphed. Decoy it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Cho'Gath Rupture: 6s flat, 950 range — telegraphed, so sidestep and punish. - Feral Scream: 11s silence at rank 1, and it shuts off your clone. - Feast: 80s at rank 1, true damage — stay above the threshold.

edits.before: Telegraphed. Decoy it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: 6s flat and 950 range — telegraphed, so sidestep and punish it.

edits.before: Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Feral Scream is 11s and silences — no clone, no Nimbus Strike.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 4/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Rupture and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 5.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Rupture and how disciplined your pattern is.

edits.before: Favoured matchup — difficulty 4/10, Cho'Gath carry threat 6/10.
edits.after: Even matchup — difficulty 5.5/10, Cho'Gath carry threat 6/10.

edits.before: Cho'Gath hits his true spike at 6 when Feast becomes an execute, so respect it hard. If you are below the Feast threshold you can be point-and-click deleted, so track his stacks and back off when you dip low.
edits.after: Cho'Gath hits his true spike at 6: Feast is 80s at rank 1 and deals true damage, so resistances do not save you. Below its threshold you are point-and-click deleted — track it and back off when you dip low.

notes: Best-written entry in the slice on prose quality — the spikes and whys were specific and correct. The failure was structural: the chart contradicted its own explanations on six of seven rows, and the header carried diff HARD with a 4/10 rating, a green tone and a 'Favoured matchup' report line all at once. Aligned to the mirror's EVEN 5.5/10. Did NOT assert grounding on Rupture: the kit file tags it, but the mirror identified that as a tooltip-parse misfire on the words 'Ruptures the ground'.
